record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: Among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, which graph has maximum energy E(G), defined as the sum of the absolute values of the adjacency eigenvalues? More specifically, is the maximum attained by the cycle C_n when n <= 7 and n is not 4, and also when n = 9, 10, 11, 13, or 15; by Lol_4,3 when n = 4; and by the lollipop graph Lol_n,6 for all other n, where Lol_n,g is formed by joining a cycle C_g to a path P_(n-g) by a single edge between a cycle vertex and a path endpoint?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.2 Among unicyclic graphs on n vertices the cycle Cn has maximal energy if n <= 7 and n = 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15. For all other values of n the unicyclic graph with maximum energy is the lollipop Loln,6.

Theorem 5.5 Among all unicyclic graphs on n vertices, the cycle Cn has maximal energy if n <= 7 but n != 4, and n = 9, 10, 11, 13 and 15; Lol4,3 has maximal energy if n = 4. For all other values of n, the unicyclic graph with maximal energy is Loln,6.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph and let λ_1, λ_2, …, λ_n be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. The energy of G is defined by
   E(G) = Σ_{i=1}^{n} |λ_i|.
A graph is called unicyclic if it is connected and contains exactly one cycle (equivalently, has n vertices and n edges). For integers n ≥ g ≥ 3, the lollipop graph Lol_{n,g} is the unicyclic graph on n vertices obtained from a cycle C_g and a path P_{n−g} by adding a single edge between one vertex of the cycle and an endpoint of the path.

Determine the unicyclic graph on n vertices that maximizes E(G). Specifically, prove or disprove that the maximum is attained by:
 (a) the cycle C_n, when n ∈ {3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15};
 (b) the lollipop Lol_{4,3}, when n = 4;
 (c) the lollipop Lol_{n,6}, for all other values of n ≥ 8.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture on the maximum-energy unicyclic graph was completely settled by Huo, Li, and Shi (2011), "Complete solution to a conjecture on the maximal energy of unicyclic graphs" (Eur. J. Combin. / arXiv:1011.4658), using the Coulson integral formula and combinatorial estimates, confirming that Lol_{n,6} (denoted P_n^6 in their notation) is the maximizer for all n ∈ {8, 12, 14} and n ≥ 16, while C_n is the maximizer in the remaining listed cases and Lol_{4,3} when n = 4.

status_evidence.title: Complete solution to a conjecture on the maximal energy of unicyclic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Caporossi et al. conjectured the unicyclic graph with maximal energy is C_n if n≤7 and n=9,10,11,13,15, and P_n^6 otherwise. We completely solve this conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture identifying the unicyclic graph of maximum energy has been completely proved.
